answer: Behavioral trail correlation. Each agent action appends to a temporal thread tied to its identity; a detector retroactively links accounts whose action timing, tool-use sequences, and network paths overlap beyond chance, flagging clusters as one operator. Because the detector runs after the fact, an attacker must sustain many genuinely independent behavior histories—a relic of separate hardware, separate schedules, separate usage—rather than one synthesized past. Like cracks surfacing in a glacier, partial separation shows up late but reliably.
